papers.title: Non-canonical microproteins as targets for shared-antigen cancer immunotherapy.
papers.authors: Fierro-Monti I.
papers.abstract: Recent research reveals that microproteins encoded by non-canonical open reading frames (ncORFs) substantially enrich the cancer immunopeptidome, driven by oncogenic stress, essential cellular functions, immune tolerance mechanisms, and antigen-processing biases. These microproteins, often critical for tumour survival, produce peptides presented on tumour cell surfaces, offering shared antigen targets for immunotherapy, particularly in tumours with low mutational burden. Here we integrate multi-level evidence demonstrating how translational reprogramming under stress, essentiality constraints limiting antigen loss, and selective antigen processing converge to promote ncORF-derived peptide presentation. While emerging data suggest immunogenicity of some microproteins, clinical validation remains pending. Advancing therapeutic applications requires development of specialised computational predictors, rigorous immunopeptidomics workflows, and prospective thymic peptide profiling to ensure efficacy and safety. This framework highlights ncORF-derived microproteins as promising yet complex targets, expanding the landscape of cancer immunotherapy beyond canonical neoantigens.

papers.title: Long-read RNA sequencing reveals full-length HERV transcripts and novel ERVE-4 isoforms with potential immunotherapeutic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Cherkasova EA, Hill T, Barisic S, Chen L, Diemer J, Redekar N, Childs RW.
papers.abstract: Introduction Human endogenous retroviruses (HERVs) are increasingly recognized as sources of tumor-associated antigens and potential targets for cellular immunotherapy. However, their repetitive sequences and noncanonical splicing patterns complicate accurate transcript annotation using common short-read RNA sequencing. This study aimed to improve HERV transcriptome annotation using long-read RNA sequencing. Methods We developed a bioinformatics workflow for comprehensive annotation of HERV expression using long-read RNA sequencing, with validation using short-read RNA sequencing. We applied this workflow to ERVE-4, a HERV element previously shown to be selectively expressed in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and to encode immunogenic peptides currently under clinical investigation as targets for cellular immunotherapy. Results Long-read sequencing captured full-length HERV transcripts, improved mapping across repetitive regions, and enabled reconstruction of HERV isoforms. The workflow identified hundreds of HERV loci in long-read datasets absent from corresponding short-read annotations. Analysis of ERVE-4 revealed previously uncharacterized isoforms, whose expression was validated across multiple ccRCC tumors using RT-dPCR. Discussion Long-read RNA sequencing improves the resolution and completeness of HERV transcriptome annotation. Novel ERVE-4 isoforms substantially expand the known antigenic coding potential of ERVE-4 possibly implying discovery of novel peptide targets for immunotherapy in ccRCC.

papers.title: Lipids at the meningeal-tumor interface: aging, anatomical niches, and meningioma biology.
papers.authors: Cerasuolo M, Raccagni NG, Laguardia S, Barahona Rodriguez GA.
papers.abstract: Meningiomas exhibit substantial molecular, anatomical, and microenvironmental heterogeneity, yet the spatial organization of their lipid biology remains poorly understood. Emerging lipidomic studies demonstrate extensive remodeling of membrane, signaling, and mitochondrial lipid classes, with profiles varying according to molecular genotype, histopathological grade, and potentially patient characteristics. In parallel, developmental, single-cell, and spatial studies have revealed the meninges and meningiomas as regionally organized systems comprising distinct stromal, vascular, immune, and neoplastic populations. Here, we integrate these lines of evidence and propose the aging meningeal lipid niche as an anatomically grounded framework for understanding lipid biology across the meningioma-meningeal interface. We examine the dural attachment and tumor-bone interface, perivascular niche, immune-enriched regions, tumor core, and tumor-brain boundary as candidate metabolic compartments in which cellular composition, vascular access, extracellular architecture, and inflammatory signaling may shape local lipid states. We further consider how aging may modify these environments through remodeling of the meningeal extracellular matrix, lymphatic function, immune composition, and lipid homeostasis, while distinguishing direct evidence in meningioma from mechanistic inference. A central limitation of current studies is their reliance on bulk tissue, which precludes confident attribution of lipid signals to specific anatomical and cellular sources. We therefore outline a spatially resolved strategy integrating anatomically registered sampling with mass spectrometry imaging, histopathology, molecular classification, and single-cell or spatial transcriptomic approaches. This framework provides testable hypotheses to determine whether meningioma lipid states reflect tumor-intrinsic programs, anatomically defined microenvironments, aging-associated remodeling, or interactions among these determinants, and how these states relate to invasion, recurrence, edema, and treatment resistance.

papers.title: Targeting cardiovascular immunometabolism with phytomedicines: an emerging therapeutic technique.
papers.authors: Balkrishna A, Mishra S, Rana M, Arya V, Singh S.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) continue to be leading causes of morbidity and death globally, with chronic inflammation contributing to disease progression and residual cardiovascular risk despite breakthroughs in conventional treatment. Immunometabolism, defined as the bidirectional connection of cellular metabolism and immune-cell activity, is an emerging approach for understanding the relationship between metabolic failure and cardiovascular inflammation. Several regulatory pathways, such as AMPK, mTOR, NLRP3, SIRT1, and NRF2, have been linked to metabolic and inflammatory responses in CVD. This review critically assesses the molecular evidence relating these pathways to CVD and investigates the potential for specific phytochemicals and phytomedicines to modify cardiovascular immunometabolism. Curcumin, resveratrol, berberine, quercetin, and andrographolide have all been shown to have pathway-specific effects in cellular and animal models of inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, macrophage responses, and endothelial dysfunction. However, mechanistic activity should not be confused with demonstrated cardiovascular therapeutic effectiveness. Poor bioavailability, phytochemical variability, insufficient standardisation, pharmacokinetic uncertainty, possible herb-drug interactions, and a lack of sufficiently powered randomised clinical studies continue to impede translation. Future research should focus on standardised formulations, mechanistic validation in relevant cardiovascular models, pharmacokinetic and safety characterisation, and well-designed clinical trials combining immunometabolic biomarkers. The integration of multi-omics, systems pharmacology, nanophytomedicine, and computational techniques may help to advance evidence-based phytopharmaceutical development.

papers.title: Systems biology prioritizes drug candidates for an interferon-response-high monocyte state in idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.authors: Haque MM, Bae J, Nila IS, Kang K, Yoon J, Kim S, Park KS.
papers.abstract: Background Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is an age-associated neurological disorder characterized by gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary dysfunction. Although cerebrospinal fluid dynamics are central to its pathophysiology, the contribution of peripheral immune alterations remains poorly understood. We characterized an interferon-response-high monocyte state observed in iNPH and evaluated computational compound prioritization. Methods We used a fixed set of marker criteria to characterize the IFN-response-high monocyte state. We then compared monocyte clusters 5 and 0 and used 150 upregulated and 150 downregulated genes to screen compounds in LINCS. We tested whether candidate rankings changed with different state definitions, comparison groups, gene-list sizes, clustering settings, and inclusion of all patients. We also repeated the queries after excluding each donor while retaining the original cell-state labels and compared the results with 100 expression-matched random gene signatures. External blood datasets and paired blood-ventricular CSF samples provided additional context. Results The marker rule classified 3,195 of 22,197 canonical monocytes as IFN-response-high. The cluster contrast identified 1,231 FDR-significant genes. Of 1,376 THP1 compounds, 138 met the operational criteria of normalized connectivity score (NCS) Conclusion This study characterizes an interferon-response-high classical-monocyte state observed within an iNPH cohort and nominates compounds with predicted inverse connectivity for experimental testing. Computational support was more consistent for rosuvastatin than for roflumilast. These findings support further investigation of peripheral innate immune states observed in an iNPH cohort and provide experimentally testable hypotheses for therapeutic repurposing.

papers.title: Acute priming using elevated fluid viscosity recovers young-like single-cell surveillance behaviors in aged human T cells.
papers.authors: Dance YW, Amitrano A, Macaluso NC, Min C, Thompson LT, Saffron AM, Ge Z, Smith IM, Ezenwanne C, Milcik N, Fennell A, Pyndell KA, Szczesny C, Langdon J, Ursitti JA, Ward CW, Stroka KM, Walston JD, Sun SX, Konstantopoulos K, Phillip JM.
papers.abstract: Aging is a complex biological process often characterized by increased vulnerability to disease, infection, and death. This increased vulnerability is mechanistically linked to a progressive and functional decline of the immune system. In humans, aged T cells lose their ability to effectively surveil complex microenvironments, thereby decreasing their capacity to clear infections, eradicate diseases, and maintain physiological homeostasis. However, specific mechanisms by which aged T cells lose this capacity to surveil remain unclear. Here, we profile three core characteristics of T cell surveillance at single-cell resolution, specifically migration, deformability, and sensing. While aged human T cells retain their capacity to migrate ex vivo, they exhibit impaired cellular deformability and deficiencies in sensing local biological signals. To modulate this surveillance defect, we perform mechanical reprogramming using elevated fluid viscosity. Results indicate that acute priming of aged T cells with elevated fluid viscosity recovers a transient young-like surveillance phenotype, particularly within CD4 + memory T cell populations. This recovered young-like phenotype is mechanistically linked to elevated SDF-1α receptor expression together with increased membrane tension, cortical F-actin, and Arp3 expression. Altogether, these findings identify a key source of surveillance defects among aged T cells and offer an effective mechano-inducible strategy for modulating single-cell behaviors.

papers.title: Clinical And Radiological Predictors of Pathological Response to Chemo-Immunotherapy in Surgically Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.authors: Cannone G, Lione L, Rosa E, Michielin A, Visonà M, Verzeletti V, Bonis A, De Silvestro M, Comacchio G, Calabrese F, Pasello G, Bonanno L, Giraudo C, Gregori D, Schiavon M, Dell'Amore A.
papers.abstract: Background Chemo-immunotherapy has shifted the treatment paradigm for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (aNSCLC), improving complete pathological response (CPR) and radical resection rates. However, preoperative parameters to predict pathological response (PR) and tailor surgical strategy are lacking. This study aimed to develop an integrated clinico-radiological model to predict PR to neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy. Methods Pre-treatment contrast chest-CT radiomic features were integrated with clinical variables and PET-CT metabolic parameters. PR was classified as CPR, major pathological response (MPR), or non-response (NR). A multistep machine learning approach using penalized multinomial regression and a random forest (RF) classifier was developed and assessed via internal cross-validation and multiclass AUC. Results We retrospectively evaluated 83 patients with aNSCLC undergoing neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy and surgery between 2017 and 2025 (18 excluded due to lack of contrast CT). Most patients (74%) were stage IIIA-IIIB; lobectomy was performed in 80%. Pathological examination revealed CPR in 41.5%, MPR in 26.2%, and NR in 32.3% of cases. The integrated clinical-radiomic RF model achieved good discrimination among PR categories, yielding a macro-averaged mean AUC of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.72-0.97). Radiomic texture features reflecting tumor heterogeneity emerged as the strongest predictors of PR. Conclusion Preoperative prediction of PR after neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy is feasible using routinely available CT scans and clinical data. This integrated model provides a practical framework for surgical stratification, directly impacting patient selection and operative planning in aNSCLC.
